title: Sugar dissolving in water is a physical change
summary: When sugar dissolves in a drink, OpenStax counts that as a physical change, because the sugar is still sugar.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says a physical change alters the state or properties of matter without changing its chemical composition, meaning the identities of the substances. Dissolving sugar in coffee is one of the three examples, beside wax melting and steam turning back into liquid water. The sugar spreads out. It does not become a new substance on that account. A later section describes the dissolved molecules staying dispersed. This card is only the classification: dissolving, here, is physical rather than chemical.
